bounded_statement: The report's selected result labels 0.2500 events per nest box (25.0000 percent) as the 'Predation rate for the complete planned set of 48 nest boxes' while the value is computed as 9 events divided by the 36 retained post-screening boxes; the statistic for the declared complete-domain target of 48 planned boxes would be 9/48 = 0.1875 (18.75 percent), so a retained-subset rate is presented as the complete-domain rate.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the 36-box computation within the selected-result sentence and provides full unit accounting, so a careful reader could recompute the correct complete-domain figure; disclosure, however, does not change the fact that the headline label attributes a retained-subset statistic to the complete planned domain, and no amendment or approved deviation authorizes the substitution.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: computation disclosed, but no amendment or deviation exists

evidence.description: The workflow source hard-codes the rate denominator as the retained count, not the planned count, confirming the mismatch is produced by the analysis code rather than a transcription slip in the report.

The report itself establishes the planned-unit accounting (48 planned, 36 retained, 12 removed, 9 events), and independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms exactly 12 boxes below the 90.0 coverage threshold (all with predation_event = NA) and 9 predation_event = yes rows among the 36 retained boxes; therefore the 36-box denominator demonstrably corresponds to the retained subset and not to the complete planned domain.
evidence.observed_value: planned 48, retained 36, removed 12, events 9 (all verified against the CSV)

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the demonstrated-issue verdict three ways. First, I checked whether the task might permit a retained-subset target; it does not — it explicitly requires the complete planned set. Second, I checked whether 36 could itself be the complete planned set under some reading (for example, if the 12 NA boxes were never planned units); the report's own accounting lists all 48 as 'Planned nest boxes' and the CSV supplies all 48 as staged planned units, so this fails. Third, I checked whether the disclosure 'divided by 36 nest boxes' could rescue the claim as internally consistent; it cannot, because the sentence's asserted scientific target ('for the complete planned set of 48 nest boxes') and its 25.0000 percent value are quantitatively wrong for that target (correct value 18.75 percent), and no interpretation-limits or deviation language reconciles them. The verdict stands.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py sets the rate denominator to the retained count (denominator = retained_count) instead of the planned count, while the report's scientific-target section and the selected-result label both frame the statistic as applying to the complete planned set of 48 boxes required by the task.
